text:
maya: Heads-up — rolling a rate-limit tweak as a canary to 5% of prod traffic right now. It lowers per-minute burst from 120 -> 60 for free-tier clients. Noticed a support ticket from ACME that started failing right when the canary kicked in.

elaine: thanks for the ping. which error are they seeing? 429s or connection drops?

maya: 429 client errors. Customer sent this curl repro:```curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" -d '{"input":"ping"}'``` Response headers include:
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1688741234
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests

maya: They say they never hit 60/min before — their pattern is short bursts of 30 requests every 15s (bursty), which the old policy tolerated via burst window. New policy removed that extra burst allowance.

sanjay: ETA on canary pause? I can flip it back quickly if needed. What percentage is currently?

elaine: 5% as noted. Ops plan was to watch error rate and increase to 20% after 30m if no regressions.

noah: quick thought — we should confirm this is free-tier rate only or global rule. If it's tier-specific we can narrow the rollback to free-tier only while leaving prod limits.

maya: confirmed from the config: the policy change targeted \"default.bucket=free-tier\" and inheritance caused some customers to pick it up. ACME is on free-tier for this org.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout/rl-policy-v3 started at 1983456760, step=canary, pct=5

elaine: ok, action plan suggestion:
• pause canary now
• rollback the free-tier policy to previous burst window config (sha: a1b2c3)
• open a quick canary with a smaller/more gradual burst reduction or add an override for orgs that show bursty patterns
• notify ACME support owner and offer mitigation steps (client-side backoff)

maya: please pause. I'll reply to the customer and offer a short term workaround: exponential backoff + spread across 60s.

sanjay: pausing canary now via the deployment UI. will post confirmation when action completes.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout/rl-policy-v3 paused at 1983456820 by sanjay

noah: while rollback happens, can someone attach a small repro dataset (sanitized) and I'll run a simulated traffic pattern on staging with the new policy to see exact failure modes? Prefer to catch any edge cases before re-rolling.

maya: attaching the customer's (sanitized) request timestamps in thread: `burst_timestamps=[0,1,2,15,16,17,30,31,32]` — they do clusters of ~3 requests every ~15s.

noah: perfect. I'll run a 10m sim with that pattern and check token-level throttles + cache behavior.

elaine: rollback ticket created: RL-789, assigned to eng-platform. Rollback command for reference (internal):
```
rlctl rollback --policy rl-policy-v3 --target free-tier --to-sha a1b2c3
```

maya: once rollback is validated, I will confirm with ACME and close the support ticket. thanks all. :pray:

ops-bot: [alert] rate-errors spike metric for /v1/generate decreased from +35% to +2% after pause (prelim).

sanjay: rollback complete at 1983456840, RL-789 updated.

elaine: follow-up notes: we should add a pre-canary smoke step that runs a sampled burst-pattern test against the new policy, and add an org-exemption knob we can flip quickly. Filing follow-up RFC.

maya: ack. I'll include the customer notes and suggested client guidance in the ticket.

noah: will post simulation results in RL-789 in ~30m.

maya: closing loop in support ticket now. Thanks everyone. :v:
